rationales: Anatomy is the study of internal structure.
Histology studies tissues.
Morphology studies the form and external structure of organisms.
Physiology studies how organisms and their parts function.
Sulphur is not the element that regulates stomatal opening and closing.
Potassium regulates the opening and closing of stomata.
Calcium is not the expected answer for stomatal regulation in this question.
Phosphorus does not regulate stomatal opening and closing.
Forestry concerns the management and use of forests.
Farming deals with developing and maintaining farms.
Horticulture focuses on cultivating fruits, vegetables, and ornamental plants.
Animal husbandry focuses on breeding and caring for animals.
Hydrogen makes up about 10% of the mass of living organisms, not 18%.
Carbon makes up about 18% of the mass of living organisms.
Oxygen makes up about 65% of the mass of living organisms, not 18%.
Nitrogen makes up about 3% of the mass of living organisms, not 18%.
Observation is the starting and most basic step of the biological method.
Deduction draws a specific conclusion from a hypothesis or general principle.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation formed after observations.
Experimentation tests a hypothesis and follows earlier steps.
Prions are not carbohydrates.
Prions are infectious protein particles.
Prions are not fats.
Prions are not minerals.
ATP is the major energy currency of cells.
FAD is an electron carrier, not the main energy currency.
Sunlight is an energy source for photosynthesis, not the energy currency used by all cells.
NAD is an electron carrier, not the main energy currency.
Louis Pasteur did not first describe cells.
Rudolf Virchow contributed to cell theory but did not first describe cells.
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus, not cells themselves.
Robert Hooke first described cells after observing cork.
Ribosomes occur in both plant and animal cells.
Mitochondria occur in both plant and animal cells.
Plastids occur in plant and algal cells, not animal cells.
Endoplasmic reticulum occurs in both plant and animal cells.
Mitosis can contribute to regeneration.
Mitosis replaces worn-out or damaged cells.
Mitosis supports growth and development.
Halving the chromosome number is a result of meiosis, not mitosis.
A cofactor does not increase activation energy as its role.
Breaking hydrogen bonds in proteins is not the general function of a cofactor.
A cofactor helps and facilitates enzyme activity.
Cofactors are non-protein components, unlike enzymes themselves.

The stated approximate coverage is not 1–4%.
The stated approximate coverage is not 1–5%.
Vitamin A does not perform this mineral-absorption and bone-deposition role.
Vitamin B is not the vitamin responsible for this role.
Vitamin C assists absorption of some minerals but is not the expected answer here.
Vitamin D promotes mineral absorption from the intestine and deposition in bones.

The expected approximate haemoglobin content is not 95%.
The cytoplasm is not entirely haemoglobin.
The biosphere is the global zone of life, not the diversity of plants.
A community consists of interacting populations of different species.
Flora refers to the plant life of a region or area.
Fauna refers to the animal life of a region or area.
